citation: Stramma, L. (1992), The South Indian Ocean Current, Journal of Physical Oceanography 22, 421–430

source_identity.access: Previously retained institutional original; all ten scanned pages visually read for this review. Earlier acquisition and scope-audit records retain their historical access descriptions.
source_identity.copyright: American Meteorological Society, 1992. No redistribution permission inferred. Original PDF, scans and private review renders are not included in this change.

review_kind: Paraphrased source findings; no figure digitization, new measured geometry or copied table

findings.finding: The author explicitly leaves current-width detail unresolved at the station resolution available.
Adjacent hydrographic stations bracket the subtropical front. Censored arrows indicate that the front lies south of the last station.
findings.measurement_consequence: Front-location brackets and their station spacing are not current edges or widths.

findings.finding: Surface geostrophic velocities average between station pairs and can underestimate a localized maximum. Station gaps reach approximately 430 km.
findings.measurement_consequence: Contour appearance cannot establish finely resolved physical edges.

findings.finding: The table describes maximum surface geostrophic velocity and upper-1000 m transports. Some northern integration bounds follow section termination or flow reversal.
findings.measurement_consequence: Neither the integration bounds nor a transport divided by an assumed speed supplies a measured width.

findings.finding: The Discovery May 1934 western oblique section diagnoses northeastward geostrophic flow relative to a deep reference. Its geography lies in the western reach subsequently separated as Agulhas Return under later naming conventions.
findings.measurement_consequence: Do not transfer a western section into the eastern South Indian Current width record, or compare its perpendicular geostrophic component directly with a 2013 model eastward component.

findings.finding: The Diamantina section near 110 E has westward frontal flow.
findings.measurement_consequence: A temperature or salinity front alone does not identify the eastward South Indian Current.

findings.finding: The 65 E section distinguishes South Indian Current flow north of the front from a stronger ACC band farther south. In the broader 60–90 E region the bands can approach and exchange water.
findings.measurement_consequence: The largest positive velocity peak in a meridional section is not automatically the South Indian Current.

findings.finding: The transport and flow depiction is a schematic assembled from hydrographic sections at different times.
findings.measurement_consequence: No observed centerline, path length or current footprint digitized from the schematic.

findings.finding: Deep density-reference choices depend on section and water mass. A shallow common reference can underestimate transport.
findings.measurement_consequence: Model total velocities at 15 m and 1000 m are not equivalent to the paper's deep-referenced geostrophic velocities or an upper-1000 m mean.

findings.finding: The station inventory includes a March 1975 Shirshov section, shallower than the sections retained for the transport schematic.
findings.measurement_consequence: Do not assign the same generalized historical period to every individual section.

findings.finding: The Eltanin entry combines an 80–88 E section context.
findings.measurement_consequence: It is not one simultaneous 80 E profile and cannot validate a specific 2013 monthly profile.

findings.finding: Eastern flow branches and turns northeastward; the paper does not establish a permanent continuous South Indian Current extension south of Australia.
findings.measurement_consequence: Do not extend endpoints merely to complete a global route.

next_source_step: Paired, dated model velocity and hydrography at 80 E, retaining neighboring native meridians, common valid times, exact depth identity and all months; separate feature-association assessment before physical-width estimation.
